title: Fruit Into Baskets
statement:
A farmer's orchard has `n` trees in a row, numbered `0` to `n - 1`. Tree `i` bears fruit of type `fruit[i]`.

You carry exactly two baskets. Each basket can hold any amount of fruit, but only of **one type**. You pick a starting tree of your choice and then move right one tree at a time, and the rules are:

- You must pick exactly one fruit from every tree you pass, starting with the tree where you begin.
- Each picked fruit has to go into a basket that is empty or already holds that type. You may not skip a tree.
- As soon as you reach a tree whose fruit fits in neither basket, you must stop (you cannot pick it). You also stop after the last tree.

Return the **maximum number of fruits** you can pick over all possible starting trees. Equivalently, find the length of the longest contiguous stretch of trees containing at most two distinct fruit types.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `fruit[0] ... fruit[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the maximum number of fruits you can pick.

examples.explanation: Starting at tree 0 you pick types 3, 1, 1, 3 (two types) and must stop at the tree with type 2. Starting at tree 3 you pick only 3, 2, 2, which is 3 fruits. The best is 4.
Start at tree 2: 6, 7, 7, 7, 6 uses only types 6 and 7, giving 5 fruits. Starting earlier fails at the 7 after 5, 5, 6.
Every tree has a different type, so from any start you can pick two fruits and must stop at the third type.

hints: The answer is the longest window of the array that contains at most two distinct values.
Grow a window to the right and keep a small map from fruit type to its count inside the window.
When the map has three types, advance the left end (decrementing counts, deleting types that reach zero) until only two remain.
